w10_T4_003759: In the morning, Hana had 109 dollars saved, more than her cousin Rin's dozen or so dollars in a piggy bank. By midday, she spent 75 dollars on new soccer cleats. In the afternoon, a tournament prize multiplied her remaining cash eightfold. By evening, a bonus round multiplied it sixfold again. Later that evening, she paid 1,233 dollars toward a family trip fund. Overnight, a matching family contribution multiplied whatever was left threefold. The next morning, a relative added 71 more dollars. How much money did Hana have after that?
w10_T4_003761: A movie theater had 189 tickets left for a midnight premiere, while a different theater across town had sold out its 400-seat house completely. A group cancellation freed up 108 tickets. A last-minute rush then bought 70 tickets, using up the fresh availability. A matching promotion multiplied the remaining ticket total eightfold to represent a giveaway pool. Finally, 50 more tickets were added from a sponsor's reserved block. How many tickets were in the pool by showtime?
w10_T4_003765: In the morning, Zara had 78 stickers, more than her friend Yara's 15. By midday, she earned 72 more stickers from a reading challenge. In the afternoon, she split her stickers evenly among three notebooks, and this story follows only the first notebook. By evening, a teacher added 51 more stickers to that notebook. Later that evening, she traded away 93 stickers to a classmate for a rare sticker she wanted. Overnight, she found 21 more stickers in a drawer. How many stickers were in that notebook by the next morning?
w10_T4_003766: In the morning, a candle shop made 32 candles, while a completely unrelated soap shop next door made 500 bars of soap. By midday, a bulk order multiplied the candle count fivefold. In the afternoon, a wholesale deal multiplied it ninefold again. By evening, the candles were split evenly among six gift boxes, and this story follows only one box. Overnight, that box's candles were divided evenly among six smaller sample packs, and only one sample pack continued. The next morning, a final shipment added 75 more candles to that pack. How many candles were in that sample pack?
w10_T4_003768: A stadium had 231 parking spots reserved for a game, while a dozen unrelated spots were reserved just for staff at a different gate. A group of 52 season-ticket holders parked early. Then 66 more cars arrived for pregame tailgating. Later, 44 spots were released back when a bus group canceled. A halftime rush then multiplied the number of occupied spots sixfold as overflow lots opened up. Finally, 41 more cars parked during the final quarter. How many cars were parked by the end of the game?
w10_T4_003770: In the morning, Diego had 143 minutes of screen time allowed, just under two and a half hours, more than his brother Mateo's 60 minutes. By midday, he had used up 128 minutes on games. In the afternoon, a reward for finishing chores added 35 more minutes. By evening, a weekend bonus multiplied his remaining minutes eightfold. Overnight, a holiday bonus multiplied it fourfold again. How many minutes of screen time did Diego have?
w10_T4_003771: In the morning, a food truck had 74 hot dogs prepped. By midday, 68 were sold during the lunch rush. In the early afternoon, 1 hot dog fell on the ground and had to be thrown out. By late afternoon, the crew prepped 18 more for the dinner crowd. By evening, 3 more were given away to a hungry street performer. How many hot dogs were left by closing?
w10_T4_003775: Amara had 182 dollars saved for a trip, more than her friend Zoe's 70, even though a completely unrelated fund at Amara's school held 5,000 dollars for scholarships. She spent 95 dollars on a plane ticket deposit. A relative then gave her 48 more dollars. A currency exchange bonus multiplied her remaining cash fivefold at the airport. She found 31 more dollars in an old wallet. Finally, she paid 481 dollars for a hotel booking. How much money did Amara have left?
w10_T4_003779: Kai had 89 dollars in a coin collection's cash value, more than his friend Ren's 30. A rare-coin appraisal multiplied the collection's value eightfold. He then sold 332 dollars worth of duplicate coins. A birthday gift added 47 dollars worth of coins. A second appraisal after a big auction multiplied the value eightfold again. He then sold off 1,392 dollars worth of coins to fund a trip. Finally, he received 60 more dollars from a coin swap. How much was Kai's collection worth at the end?
w10_T4_003781: Priya had 235 dollars, or 23,500 cents as her little sister liked to compute, more than her friend Sana's dozen dollars in coins. She spent 142 dollars on a new laptop case and accessories. A cashback reward then multiplied her remaining balance sixfold. A second reward multiplied it fivefold again. A tax refund added 65 more dollars. Finally, a matching investment bonus multiplied her balance eightfold. How much money did Priya have at the end?
w10_T4_003782: A bookstore had 91 novels on a clearance shelf, plus a dozen magazines stacked separately that don't count here. A publisher's return policy multiplied the clearance shelf fivefold overnight. A donation added 24 more novels. A book club dropped off 18 more. A school library contributed 41 more, and a final estate sale added 60 more. Finally, 497 novels were sold during a weekend clearance event. How many novels were left on the shelf?
w10_T4_003791: Ethan had 144 baseball cards, more than his cousin Owen's 50. A booster-box event multiplied his collection sevenfold. A second matching event multiplied it sevenfold again. A trade with a classmate added 71 more cards, and a gift from his uncle added 39 more. How many cards did Ethan have in total?
w10_T4_003796: A warehouse had 204 boxes of canned vegetables, while a separate section held 3,000 boxes of canned fruit. A rush order multiplied the vegetable-box count fourfold. A shipment of 723 boxes then went out to a grocery chain. A restock multiplied the remaining boxes sixfold. A late delivery added 43 more boxes, and a final donation added 29 more. How many boxes of canned vegetables were in the warehouse?
w10_T4_003797: A charity had 211 dollars, or 21,100 cents as the treasurer liked to note, in its account at the start of the drive. A local business donated 34 more dollars. A matching-donor event then multiplied the account sevenfold. A second matching event multiplied it fourfold again. Finally, the charity spent 3,655 dollars on a community center renovation. How much money was left in the account?
w10_T4_003798: In the morning, Mika had 141 dollars in savings, more than her coworker Dana's 60. By midday, a bonus multiplied her savings fivefold. In the afternoon, a second bonus multiplied it sixfold again. By evening, a rebate added 45 more dollars. That night, she paid 1,084 dollars for a security deposit on an apartment. The next morning, a matching family gift multiplied what remained eightfold. That afternoon, she paid 20,567 dollars for a used car in cash. How much money did Mika have left?
w10_T4_003804: In the morning, Sofia had 232 dollars saved, more than her roommate Elle's 90. By midday, her paycheck added 55 more dollars. In the afternoon, she paid a 4-dollar transaction fee. By evening, a refund added 74 dollars, and a rebate check brought in 69 more. That night, a matching employer contribution doubled her total. The next morning, interest added 48 more dollars. How much money did Sofia have?
w10_T4_003806: In the morning, a lemonade stand had 36 dollars in its cash box, or 3,600 cents as the kids liked to count it out. By midday, a busy morning added 56 more dollars. In the afternoon, a matching donation from a parent tripled the cash box. By evening, a tip jar added 11 more dollars. That night, the family paid 206 dollars for new supplies. The next morning, a franchise deal multiplied the remaining cash ninefold. Later that day, a 25-dollar fee was paid to a permit office. How much money was in the cash box?
w10_T4_003808: Noor had 45 stickers, more than her friend Talia's 15. She split her stickers evenly among five pages in a sticker book, and this story follows only the first page. A sticker-trading event multiplied that page's stickers fivefold. A second trade multiplied it threefold again. A teacher then added 35 more stickers to that page. Finally, a school-wide bonus multiplied the page's stickers sevenfold. How many stickers were on that page in the end?
w10_T4_003809: Malik had 223 dollars, more than his cousin Femi's 90. He spent 3 dollars on a snack. He then split his remaining cash evenly with his brother, keeping only his own half. He spent 81 dollars on a new game and 24 dollars on a movie ticket. Finally, his grandmother gave him 67 more dollars. How much money did Malik have in the end?
w10_T4_003816: In the morning, a warehouse had 190 boxes of school supplies. By midday, a matching donation multiplied the box count ninefold. In the afternoon, 730 boxes were shipped out to schools in need. By evening, a late delivery added 40 more boxes. Overnight, a large order removed 954 boxes for a district-wide distribution. The next morning, a final donation added 71 more boxes. How many boxes were in the warehouse?
w10_T4_003820: Zoe had 78 dollars, more than her friend Ivy's dozen or so. She spent 77 dollars on a new backpack for school. A cashback reward then multiplied her remaining dollar ninefold. She paid a 2-dollar processing fee. Her aunt gave her 53 more dollars, and a rebate check added 49 more. How much money did Zoe have at the end?
w10_T4_003823: Diego had 142 dollars, more than his friend Bruno's dozen or so. He spent 9 dollars on a snack. His grandmother gave him 76 more dollars. He then paid 189 dollars for a repair on his bike. He spent 13 more dollars on parts. Finally, a rebate added 62 more dollars. How much money did Diego have at the end?
w10_T4_003824: Amir had 142 dollars, or 14,200 cents as his sister liked to calculate, more than his friend Zaid's 60 dollars. A weekend job multiplied his savings sixfold. A bonus multiplied it fivefold again. A third reward multiplied it threefold once more. A refund then added 78 more dollars. Finally, a matching grant multiplied his whole balance ninefold. How much money did Amir have at the end?
w10_T4_003830: A warehouse had 194 boxes of shoes, plus a dozen empty boxes stacked separately for recycling. A delivery added 27 more boxes, even though a totally different order for 5,000 boxes of socks was mentioned on the same invoice. Then 140 boxes shipped out to stores. A late return brought back 22 boxes. A matching restock doubled the total. Finally, 74 more boxes arrived from a new supplier. How many boxes of shoes were in the warehouse?
w10_T4_003832: In the morning, a bakery had 109 loaves of bread. By midday, a rush order multiplied the loaves sevenfold, even though a different bakery across town reported baking 2,000 loaves that same morning. In the afternoon, 603 loaves were sold to a catering company. By evening, a matching order tripled the remaining loaves. Overnight, a final wholesale deal multiplied the loaves eightfold. How many loaves were in the bakery by the next morning?
